name: Blood and soil
summary: Blood and soil (Blut und Boden) is the idea that a people defined by hereditary blood is bound to the land it works, with the free peasant farm as the source of the nation's life. Popularised by Richard Walther Darre, it called for a new hereditary elite, eugenic marriage rules, inherited family farms and a turn away from industry, cities, liberalism and Marxism. It became the motto of Nazi Germany's agrarian estate and the basis of the 1933 Hereditary Farm Law.
scope: The blood and soil doctrine as set out by Darre in A New Nobility of Blood and Soil (1930), as described in Bramwell's biography, and as put into practice in the Hereditary Farm Law of 1933 and the Reichsnaehrstand. It does not cover Nazism as a whole, Hitler's other policies, other uses of the phrase (Zionist, white nationalist) or the Artaman League beyond Darre's own writings.
